content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus forward steps: Starting from simple building blocks: maybe 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) for first phenyl ring with methyl; sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-chlorobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually target has sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings: an aniline (p-tolyl) attached to sulfonyl group attached to another phenyl bearing the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain.

So retrosynthesis: Break amide bond: gives carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (anilide). That acid is from Doebner modification of aromatic aldehyde (p-chlorobenzaldehyde?) Wait the side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached to phenyl sulfonyl group. The unsaturated chain attached to phenyl via double bond to carbonyl amide to an aniline (anilide). The phenyl bearing the sulfonyl is c2ccc(... )cc2 with substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So the unsaturated acid precursor is p-chlorobenzaldehyde? Actually the phenyl ring attached to sulfonyl has a para substituent of the unsaturated chain. The chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl (aniline). The unsaturated acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) would be p-chlorobenzaldehyde + malonic acid -> p-chlorophenylacrylic acid (p-chlorocinnamic acid). Then amide formation with aniline (c3ccccc3N) gives p-chlorophenylacrylamide. Then sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (p-methylbenzenesulfonyl chloride) reacting with aniline (the first phenyl ring) to give sulfonamide linking the two phenyls? Actually target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide connects p-tolyl amine (the first phenyl) to sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So sulfonyl chloride is p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? Wait sulfonyl chloride would be p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl). Reaction with aniline (the second phenyl? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So the sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl (p-chlorophenyl sulfonyl chloride). But the second phenyl also has the unsaturated amide substituent. So sulfonyl chloride must be p-chlorophenyl sulfonyl chloride (Cl-Ph-SO2Cl) then react with p-toluidine (CH3-Ph-NH2) to give sulfonamide linking them. However the second phenyl also has the unsaturated amide substituent; that substituent is attached at para position relative to sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl chloride must be p-chlorophenyl sulfonyl chloride with that substituent already present (i.e., p-(α,β-unsaturated amide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride). But we can consider retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide bond to give p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) bearing the unsaturated amide side chain. That sulfonyl chloride can be derived from the corresponding sulfonic acid (aryl sulfonic acid) via chlorination, but we may ignore that step.

Thus three steps: 1) amide formation (break amide) -> unsaturated acid + aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) Doebner modification (break C=C double bond) -> aromatic aldehyde (p-chlorobenzaldehyde) + malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation (break N-S bond) -> p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (p-chlorophenyl sulfonyl chloride). The sulfonyl chloride already has the unsaturated acid attached? Actually after step 2 we have p-chlorocinnamic acid (p-chlorophenylacrylic acid). Then step 1 amide formation with aniline gives p-chlorophenylacrylamide (attached to aniline). Then step 3 sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride derived from that amide? Wait the sulfonyl chloride must be attached to the phenyl bearing the amide side chain. So we need a sulfonyl chloride that is p-chlorophenyl sulfonyl chloride with the amide side chain attached at para position. That could be obtained from the amide product by sulfonyl chloride formation (chlorination of sulfonic acid). But the guidance only mentions sulfonamide formation as a step, not sulfonyl chloride synthesis. So we assume the sulfonyl chloride is available as a building block (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So the retrosynthesis: target -> break sulfonamide -> gives p-toluidine (starting material) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (with unsaturated amide side chain). Then break amide -> gives unsaturated acid (p-chlorocinnamic acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break C=C via Doebner -> gives p-chlorobenzaldehyde and malonic acid (or malonic acid derivative). So three steps.

We need to produce JSON route with nested reactions.

We need template IDs for each step. We have some template IDs from search results: For amide formation (break amide) we need a template that breaks amide to give carboxylic acid and amine. Search didn't find but we can maybe use template ID 514 (retro_smarts for amide cleavage). That template: '[O;D1;H0:2]=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[c:3])-[NH;D2;+0:4]-[c:5]>>O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[c:3].[NH2;D1;+0:4]-[c:5]'. This breaks amide into acid and amine. So we can use template_id 514.

For Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). Need a template that forms C=C and breaks C-C and C-O. Might be template ID 312088? That one seems to convert aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid to unsaturated acid? Let's examine: retro_smarts_template: '[O;D1;H0:4]=[C:3](-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:2])-[c:5]1:[c:6]:[c:7]:[c:8]:[c:9]:[c:10]:1>>C=C-C-[N;H0;D3;+0:1](-[c:2])-[C:3](=[O;D1;H0:4])-[c:5]1:[c:6]:[c:7]:[c:8]:[c:9]:[c:10]:1'. This seems to be reverse of amide formation? Not sure. Might be for Doebner? Another template maybe 293692? That one breaks sulfonamide? Not.

We could search for template that forms C=C from aldehyde and malonic acid. Let's search functional_groups_formed C-C double bonds, broken carboxylic acid? But we can't break carboxylic acid. Maybe template ID 514 is amide, 1313644 is sulfonamide formation (break sulfonamide). Indeed template 1313644 retro_smarts: '[C:5]-[c...]-[NH;D2;+0:12]-[S...]-[c:4]...>>Cl-[S...]-[c:4].[C:5]...-[NH2]' This is sulfonamide formation (break N-S). So we can use template_id 1313644 for sulfonamide step.

Now need Doebner modification template. Search for template that forms C=C from aldehyde and malonic acid. Let's search for functional_groups_formed ["C-C double bonds"] and broken ["carboxylic esters"] maybe? Let's try search.
